ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a five-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle, with N-H labeled at the bottom, and two double-bond lines drawn inside the ring; on the right side there is a CCl2 fragment, with electron dots and curved arrows beside it. Reasoning: According to the question, ignore the arrows and electron dots, and exclude bonds involving hydrogen, so N-H is not counted. Around the five-membered ring there are a total of 5 connecting edges between non-hydrogen atoms; the edges where double bonds are located are counted by the position of one bond and are not additionally doubled, so the ring contributes 5 bonds. In the CCl2 fragment on the right, carbon forms one C-Cl bond with each of the two chlorines, for a total of 2 bonds. The total number is 5 + 2 = 7.

raw_record.question_text:

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a five-membered heterocycle plus a CCl2 fragment. Trace only non-hydrogen bonds: count the five edges around the ring as 5 bonds, counting the double-bonded edges as bonds but not as extra separate items. Then count the two C-Cl bonds in the CCl2 fragment. Exclude the N-H bond and ignore arrows/electron dots. Sum 5 + 2 = 7.
